thread:
priya: Drafted a first-pass PRD for Dedicated Capacity v1. Link: https://redwood.internal/prds/dedicated-capacity-v1. Need sharp acceptance criteria for SLA targets, throughput sizing, and autoscaling. PTAL :wave:

mike: Thanks — tagging infra/runtime to sanity-check numbers. I can take ownership of launch criteria once we agree on SLOs. :+1:

tom: Quick thoughts: we should call out both uptime SLA and latency SLOs separately. Proposal: uptime 99.95% per region, and latency SLOs by model class (small/med/large). Also need explicit failover behavior to hosted API when capacity is exhausted.

sara: Agree. For latency SLOs propose we use token-based SLOs so it's stable across model sizes. Example targets (512-token requests):
- small (<=7B): p50 < 30ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms
- medium (7-13B): p50 < 50ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms
- large (>13B): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms, p99 < 900ms
These are for Dedicated under normal load (no autoscale events).

priya: Nice. We also need acceptance criteria that tie to observability: dashboards + alerting thresholds, and a runbook for capacity drain.

jordan: From oncall POV: include rollback/mitigation acceptance criteria:
- automatic fallback to hosted models when pool <= 20% remaining capacity for >3m
- manual failover playbook tested in staging
- incident detection for KV cache corruption and automated cache flush capability

ana: Customer ask: burst capacity is important — customers want predictable sustained throughput and occasional bursts. We should document max burst factor and throttling behavior.

tom: Sizing note: make the sizing formula explicit so sales/ops can translate commitments to GPUs. Example calculation we used in the doc:```
expected_qps = peak_rps * tail_factor (tail_factor 1.2-1.5)
qps_per_gpu = model_specific_value (see perf matrix)
required_gpus = ceil(expected_qps / qps_per_gpu) + safety_buffer
```
Add an example: if peak_rps=500, tail_factor=1.25, qps_per_gpu=80 => required_gpus=ceil(625/80)=8 (+2 buffer) => reserve 10 GPUs.

sara: For autoscale acceptance criteria: define scale reaction times and cold-start bounds. Suggested minimums:
- scale-up latency: new worker accepts traffic within 90s (target), 180s (max)
- scale-down cool-down: 2m
- cold-start latency: < 15s for warm path, < 60s for cold GPUs (depends on container image pull)
Include an autoscale policy example customers can adopt:
```
policy:
  metric: "token_rate"
  scale_up_threshold: 0.75
  scale_down_threshold: 0.30
  cool_down: 120s
  max_burst_units: 2
```

priya: Good — can someone capture these into the PRD acceptance section? I'll add the perf matrix separately.

mike: I'll take the acceptance checklist. Draft items:
- SLA: 99.95% regional uptime measured at gateway level (exclusions for scheduled maint)
- Latency SLOs: (sara's table) validated via synthetic + canary traffic
- Throughput sizing: formula + verification test that sustained qps for 30m meets target with <2% error
- Autoscale: scale-up/scale-down times within targets, tested under load in staging
- Failover: automated hosted fallback works with <5s decision latency
- Observability: dashboards and alerts in console + perf trace sampling at 1%

jordan: Edge cases to call out in the PRD:
- Rapid oscillation (scale thrash) when load is spiky -> require hysteresis and rate limits on scale ops
- Partial GPU failures / degraded nodes -> ensure graceful evict and redistribution within 60s
- Model pinning: customers pinning specific model builds must be supported even if newer build is on host pool
- KV cache warmup: when restoring large KV caches, perf degradation window must be documented and bounded

sara: Also add quantization/precision fallback: if a quantized path hits numerical issues, platform should fall back to full-precision variant automatically and alert.

ana: For customers, include SLA credit mechanics and how committed capacity vs usage overage is billed. Ops needs an example invoice sequence.

priya: I'll incorporate all of this into the acceptance criteria section and push a new draft by EOD. Please drop short comments in the doc rather than long threads here so we don't lose context.

mike: One last ask: include a minimal canary checklist that the SREs can run:
- deploy to canary pool (1% traffic) for 30m
- run synthetic latency QPS profile at declared peak for 15m
- verify no p99 regressions >10% vs baseline

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/dedicated-capacity-v1 -> staging at 2026-03-20T15:12:34Z :rocket:

priya: thanks all — I'll ping again when draft updated. :raised_hands:
